thread:
alex (infra): Heads up — proposing a rolling NIC microcode reboot for eu-west3 hosted GPU pools next Tue 04:00-07:00 UTC. We saw intermittent packet drops on a small subset of racks at ~95th pct egress; vendor microcode fixes latency spikes.

alex (infra): Plan is staggered drains by rack cohort (~8 racks per cohort), 10m drain window + 15m reboot + 10m healthcheck, backfill from eu-central and us-east if needed. Will NOT touch Dedicated/reserved pools unless we get customer opt-in.

sarah (eng-sre): Can we exclude Dedicated? customers will freak if capacity gets impacted without notice. Also, what's the estimated capacity hit for hosted?

alex (infra): Yes excluding Dedicated. Expected hosted capacity hit ~12-18% if we warm backfill across regions. We can reduce to ~8-10% with aggressive KV/prefix cache warmup. Cost delta estimate ~ $2.5k-3.5k/hr during the window if we spin extra instances.

rachel (product): Need to surface this in Console banners + status page. Product team can craft customer comms but need final schedule by EOD Friday.

mike (infra-eng): One extra risk: some racks are on switches with older firmware — vendor warned reboot may force L2 flap and a brief pod evictions beyond our drain window. Suggest extend per-rack buffer to 20m and do canary on 2 racks first.

kyle (oncall): Runbook please. Oncall needs rollback steps and an est. noise floor for alerts (SLOs). Who is primary during the window?

alex (infra): I'll be primary, mike will be secondary. Runbook (brief):
```
# drain cohort
kubectl cordon node-1 node-2 ... --context=eu-west3
kubectl drain node-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120
# tag to backfill pool
infractl pool backfill --region eu-central --capacity 12% --reason "eu-west3 nic reboot"
# healthcheck after reboot
infractl node healthcheck --node node-1 --timeout 600
# rollback if >5% pod failures or job SLA breach
infractl cancel-backfill --pool eu-central
```

alex (infra): Also setting temporary routing policy: prefer low-cost fallback models for queries flagged non-SLA to reduce token spend during backfill.

sarah (eng-sre): Agree with canary. Also add temporary alert suppression for expected eviction noise — annotate incidents with maintenance id.

mike (infra-eng): I'll add two canary racks at 04:00, we watch for L2 flaps and CPU/IO latency for 60m before widening. If switch reboots cause >30s BGP reconvergence we'll pause.

alex (infra): Updated schedule: canaries 04:00-04:40 (2 racks), then cohort cadence with 20m buffer between cohorts. Total window 04:00-09:00 UTC to accommodate backoff. Posting to infra calendar and status page.

infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: https://redwood.status/maintenance/1759999999 :calendar: (eu-west3 NIC microcode reboot)

rachel (product): Thanks — product will draft banner + email segment for paying customers. Please attach final hostlist by 16:00 PST.

kyle (oncall): I'll put a warroom channel and a short checklist for post-window verification (latency smoke, SLOs, KV hit rates, model tail latencies).

sarah (eng-sre): One more ask — measure model-level tail latency before and after; open a regression alert if p99 increases >15%.

alex (infra): Will do. I pushed a quick health dashboard link in the calendar invite. :thumbsup:

mike (infra-eng): :thumbsup: I'll start inventorying switch firmware and flag any racks that need manual vendor coord.

alex (infra): OK everyone — finalizing hostlist and will post the customer-facing comms draft by 18:00 UTC. Please ack here if you can join the warroom during the window.

sarah (eng-sre): ack

mike (infra-eng): ack

kyle (oncall): ack

rachel (product): ack
